clue.text: Couple at work have sex

indicators.note: letters set to work are busy moving about, so the phrase before is rearranged

parts.note: the two words supply all eight letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: A pair of colleagues get intimate in the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at work' looks like a place but is the signal; 'at' does double duty as fodder, so read 'Couple at' as the letters and 'work' as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To copulate is the formal biological verb for mating, the same act described plainly.

clue.text: Space traveller revealed by start of oscillation in measuring instrument

indicators.note: one piece sits in another, so it is placed inside the device's name

parts.note: a meter is a gauge that measures

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: opening letter of oscillation

explanation.surface: A spacecraft's presence is betrayed by a wobble on a dial.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is a rock hurtling through space, travelling until it burns up in the atmosphere.

clue.text: 25 of knitted jumper

indicators.note: knitted wool is worked into a new pattern, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the answer to clue 25
taken as written

explanation.surface: Remorse over a badly knitted pullover.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a pullover, which the surface uses; here it means something that jumps. 25 is REGRET.
explanation.definitionFit: Tree frogs are agile climbing amphibians famous for leaping between branches, so one counts as a jumper.

clue.text: Girl's three articles

wordplay.note: the indefinite article AN, the definite THE and the indefinite A in a row

explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl's' is 'Girl is'; the answer is a girl's name built from three articles, the grammar word for a, an and the.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthea is a female first name, so any girl so called fits the definition.

clue.text: Bird seen on migration in Tresco?

indicators.note: migrating creatures move around, so the letters of the island name shift position

parts.note: Tresco is one of the Isles of Scilly off Cornwall

explanation.surface: Birdwatchers spot a migrant on a Scilly island.
explanation.definitionFit: The scoter is a dark sea duck of northern coasts, a kind of waterfowl.

clue.text: Bird may be hitch for hikers

indicators.note: a hitch is a snag that disrupts things, so the word that follows is jumbled

parts.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A hitch-hiking walker might find a lift by bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hitch for hikers' reads as hitch-hiking, but 'hitch' is the signal acting on 'hikers'.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrike, or butcher-bird, is a songbird that impales prey on thorns.

clue.text: Birds presented with bill for geranium

parts.words: Birds presented with bill for geranium
parts.note: surface reading: someone is handed an invoice for a pot plant
setter's reading: put the word bill after these long-legged birds and you get a plant name, a wild geranium

explanation.surface: A flock is handed the invoice for a pot plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Cranesbill is the common name of the wild geranium, so these birds plus 'bill' name the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Cranes are tall wading birds with long necks and legs, the plural matching the clue.

clue.text: Hare-brained puss in pigpen

indicators.note: one thing sits in another, so the animal goes inside the pen

parts.note: a sty is an enclosure for pigs
puss is a pet name for a cat

explanation.surface: A daft cat has wandered into the pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatty is British informal for scatterbrained, absent-minded and foolish, like a mad March hare.

clue.text: What Elvis sang about — and where, too

definitions.text: What Elvis sang about — and where, too

parts.note: surface reading: the subject of one of Elvis Presley's songs, a 1960 hit from the film G.I. Blues
setter's reading: the title also names the core of a tree, a place where birds such as woodpeckers make their homes

explanation.surface: A quiz question on the subject and setting of an Elvis hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The song title doubles as the heart of a tree trunk, fitting the puzzle's bird theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden Heart was a number-one single for Elvis Presley, and its title literally describes timber at the centre of a trunk.

clue.text: Bird with belly-ache

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a plump game bird of the moors

explanation.surface: A bird with a stomach upset.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a moorland game bird; the verb means to grumble, as belly-ache does in slang.

clue.text: Giddy dove circling another bird in the air

indicators.note: a giddy creature reels and spins, so its letters are spun into a new order
circling something means going round it, so the scrambled word wraps the other bird

parts.note: dove rearranged, split around the next piece
the rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: A dizzy dove wheels around another bird high up.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhea cannot fly, a joke against 'in the air'. OVE goes before and D after the inserted bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Overhead means up above, aloft or in the sky above one's head.

clue.text: A bird — or, to put it another way, birds

indicators.note: putting something another way means rephrasing it, so the letters are arranged differently

parts.note: auks are diving seabirds such as puffins and guillemots

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher names one species, then corrects the sighting to a whole group of birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'birds' must be turned into a specific bird name before rearranging: auks.
explanation.definitionFit: The skua is a predatory gull-like seabird that harries other birds for food.

clue.text: An eccentric breeds rats for birds

indicators.note: an eccentric is odd and off-centre, so the letters that follow are disordered

parts.note: ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An oddball raises rodents as food for pet birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Redbreast is an old name for the robin, so the plural names several robins.

clue.text: Wrong note in port for seabird

indicators.note: one thing in another means it is placed inside, so the port's name wraps the rest

parts.note: Hull is a port on England's east coast
erring means going wrong
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A sailor in a harbour hits a wrong note while singing about seabirds.
explanation.walkthrough: H and ULL frame the wrong-plus-note piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The herring gull is the commonest large gull of British coasts, a typical seabird.

clue.text: Mockingbird with lyre-shaped tail

indicators.note: something shaped has been moulded into a new form, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: the rail is a marsh bird
lyre rearranged, placed as the end piece

explanation.surface: A mockingbird with a tail like a harp, as in the lyrebird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mockingbird' must be split: 'Mocking' is the definition and 'bird' the start of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Raillery is good-humoured teasing banter, so it is mocking talk as a noun.

clue.text: Outstanding feature of scenery — as well as mountain-top circled by bird

indicators.note: a thing circled by another sits within it, so the songbird goes around

parts.note: the lark is a songbird
and means as well as

indicators.note: in a down entry the top of a word is its first letter, so only that is used

parts.note: first letter of mountain

explanation.surface: A mountain summit with a bird wheeling round it stands out in the view.
explanation.definitionFit: A landmark is a prominent object in a landscape, used to find one's way.

clue.text: It's characteristic of a twitcher to follow the author of "The Raven" describing "The Raven"

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe wrote the poem The Raven
a tic is the involuntary twitch a twitcher displays

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's trait is to follow Poe's poem about a raven.
explanation.walkthrough: A twitcher is British slang for a keen birdwatcher, but here it is someone with a twitch. 'to follow' puts the twitch after the author.
explanation.definitionFit: The Raven is a famous poem, so an adjective describing it would be poetic, of or like poetry.

clue.text: A beast of burden is the first to help

parts.note: a donkey is a beast of burden
taken as written

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: opening letter of the

explanation.surface: A pack animal is always the first to lend a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to aid or support someone, the verbal sense in the infinitive.

clue.text: Bird in town centre going round to cinema providing animal shelter

indicators.note: going round means turning about, so the kept letters run backwards
the centre of a word is its middle, so only the inner letters are kept

parts.note: the inner two letters of town

indicators.note: to shelter something is to hold it inside, so the cinema wraps the beast

parts.note: Odeon is a British cinema chain, so a cinema
a pig is a farm animal

explanation.surface: A bird circles a town centre, heading for a cinema that houses animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Odeon is the name of a chain of British cinemas, so it stands for any cinema; the animal goes inside it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The wood pigeon is a large grey pigeon common in British woods and fields.

clue.text: River in southern highlands floods

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it, so the hills wrap the letter

parts.note: the North and South Downs are chalk hills of southern England
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A river bursts its banks in the hills of the south.
explanation.walkthrough: The Downs are ranges of chalk hills in southern England, not highlands in the Scottish sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To drown is to submerge or inundate, so the verb is a synonym for floods.

clue.text: Spice Girls' debut, having first met UN Assembly

indicators.note: an assembly puts parts together into a new whole, so the letters are rebuilt

parts.note: met and UN rearranged, placed first

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so only the opening letter shows

parts.note: opening letter of Girls

explanation.surface: The Spice Girls launched their career after meeting at the United Nations General Assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spice Girls' must be split: 'Spice' is the definition. 'having first' sets the rebuilt words before the debut letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmeg is a fragrant seed ground for flavouring, a classic kitchen spice.

clue.text: Kill two birds with one stone — that includes birds' birthplace

parts.note: surface padding: the start of the proverb, giving no letters

indicators.note: the phrase includes the answer, so look for it running inside the words before

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: The proverb about getting two things done with one effort.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole proverb is surface; only its last two words carry the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest is where eggs are laid and hatched, so it is where chicks are born.

clue.text: Bird seen on street in pushchair

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
the roller is a brightly coloured bird

explanation.surface: A bird is spotted riding in a baby's buggy on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the bird after the street abbreviation. A pushchair is the British word for a baby's folding buggy.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroller is the usual American and also British word for a folding pushchair for a toddler.

clue.text: A bird has to mount it

parts.note: taken as written
Mt is the abbreviation for mount
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird is obliged to climb something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' looks like a verb but is the noun, a mountain, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomtit is a familiar name for a small tit, especially the blue tit, a garden bird.

clue.text: Wine for a bird

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sweet wine from the ... Islands, once called ... sack
second meaning: a yellow songbird kept as a pet

explanation.surface: Buying a drink for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Canary was a historical sweet fortified wine from the islands, and the same name belongs to the yellow finch kept in cages.

clue.text: Ruth or Rachel's first bird

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: opening letter of Rachel
an egret is a white heron

explanation.surface: Two biblical women, with Rachel's pet bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth and Rachel both look like names from the Bible; Ruth is actually an old noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is an archaic word for sorrow or remorse, as in ruthless, matching the noun sense of regret.
